name: Pudina
actions: Cooling to the taste though warming in Ayurveda
kitchenUse: A handful of fresh leaves in chutney, raita or water, or steeped in hot water as mint tea after meals.

typicalUse.adultAmount: Food amounts; a cup or two of mint tea a day
typicalUse.note: Research on peppermint oil capsules for irritable bowel does not apply directly to kitchen mint leaves.

cautions.note: Mint can relax the valve at the top of the stomach and make acid reflux worse.
Never put mint or peppermint oil on or near a baby's or small child's face; menthol can affect their breathing.
Avoid if mint has caused an allergic reaction before.

evidence.summary: Peppermint oil capsules have reasonable evidence for easing irritable bowel symptoms; evidence for mint leaf tea is limited.

sources.title: NCCIH: Peppermint Oil: Usefulness and Safety
